paragraphs: Marta, Rav's uncle. Yuḥasin is uncertain whether Marta was a man or woman (see Shemuel bar Marta). Rashbam, Ḥezkat HaBatim 52a, writes: a sage's name, R. Ḥiyya's brother, as Yevamot says, Marta, Eivo, Ḥana and R. Ḥiyya. End of quotation. It is not in Yevamot but Sanhedrin 5a; so I later found in שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas], 'as Sanhedrin says.' See Yehoshua ben Gamla, where Marta is a woman. In Ḥezkat HaBatim above, when Rabbah bar bar Ḥana’s wife was dying she said, 'These jewels are Marta's.' Since these are women's ornaments—see Arukh, final entry kaf—it would seem that Marta was a woman and that Rabbah bar bar Ḥana left them to his aunt Marta. But Arvei Pesaḥim 103a has Marta in R. Yehoshua's name, seemingly a man's name. Jerusalem Talmud, Af Al Pi, tells of Marta, to whom the sages allotted two se'ah of wine each day, etc. Yefeh Mar'eh writes that this is not Marta bat Boethus mentioned in HaNizzakin. See above, Abba bar Marta, who is Abba bar Minyomi: this would suggest Marta was a woman, so sometimes he was called Abba bar Marta after his mother and sometimes bar Minyomi after his father. It requires examination. His sons: R. Yehoshua—requires examination—and Rav Shemuel.
